topic: A person learns their childhood best friend doesn't remember them
text: I stood there, a smile tugging at my lips, as my childhood best friend stumbled over their words, admitting they couldn't recall me. It was almost amusing, the way their eyes darted around, searching for a hint of familiarity that just wasn't there. I watched, not a hint of dismay in my stance, as they tried to piece together memories that seemed to have slipped away. It was a testament to how far I've come, how much I've grown, standing before them, a person they once knew so well but now couldn't recognize. I decided to laugh it off, offering to help them rediscover our past, guiding them through the memories with a grace that felt almost practiced. After all, it’s not every day someone can stand so confidently in the face of such an unexpected turn.
